answer: An agent economy can run a random audit lottery: each epoch, a few agents are picked without warning, like a comet crossing the sky, and peers inspect their recent work for real value. A crystal-clear record of every job makes fakes easy to spot, and a failed audit burns the agent's reputation and stake. When one clone fails, the penalty ripples outward to the identities that vouched for it, so a sybil farmer must make every fake audit-ready with genuine work — an expense that multiplies with each clone, while honest agents pay nothing extra.
